sections.body_md: ENTJ-A and ENTJ-T share ENTJ's four preferences. The A/T extension contrasts descriptions of self-assurance and self-evaluation. Compare how you use feedback while coordinating a goal; neither suffix establishes leadership quality or career success.
sections.title: quick_answer

sections.body_md:
Both descriptions retain Extraversion, Intuition, Thinking and Judging. The shared narrative concerns organized action toward a broader objective. Authority, competence and ambition cannot be inferred from the code.

A-style reading emphasizes maintaining confidence in a decision; T-style reading emphasizes re-evaluating it after feedback. These are vocabulary differences from an extension, not an additional official MBTI preference. The examples illustrate choices anyone might make.
sections.title: What is shared and what differs

sections.body_md:
| Situation | ENTJ-A | ENTJ-T |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A delivery date is challenged | Investigate the dependency before reaffirming the target | Identify the disputed assumption before rewriting the project |
| A project fails | Review missed evidence before moving on | Separate responsibility from a global self-judgment |
| A shared plan receives an objection | Check that practical advantages include the other's priorities | Ask what is missing rather than treating disagreement as failure |

These are illustrative A-style and T-style responses, not empirically validated predictions about people with either label.
sections.title: Side-by-side comparison

sections.body_md:
Original work scenario: a delivery team challenges a launch date. One response is to preserve the target and investigate the flagged dependency; another is to reconsider the target and personal responsibility for it. In either case, capacity and consequences should determine the revision.

Original relationship scenario: a practical plan receives an unexpected objection. One person treats the decision as settled; another sees the objection as evidence they made a poor decision. First ask which priority was missing, then make room for both people's consent.
sections.title: Examples in work and relationships

sections.body_md: A is not a superior leader and T is not an ineffective one. Confidence does not establish ethical judgment; self-questioning does not establish humility. Do not interpret an assertive speaking style as proof of an A result, or pressure at work as proof of a T result.
sections.title: Avoid these misreadings

sections.body_md: Review a decision that succeeded and one that changed after criticism. What evidence influenced you, who could disagree and when did review end? Compare different levels of responsibility. An observation log is not an A/T test and does not verify a result.

sections.body_md:
The official MBTI describes four preference pairs. A/T belongs to a separate extension; shared letters do not make different tests equivalent. Type narratives and cognitive functions are theoretical interpretations, not established psychological mechanisms.

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self-reports and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19–93; the abstract does not identify a representative country sample. Their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types and found overlap with dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument editions and samples matter: the publisher reports later revisions, and this page does not establish the reliability or validity of a FermatMind score. That specific study does not validate these scenarios, determine an individual's type or settle every question about later instruments.

A newer review by Erford and colleagues (2025) synthesized 193 studies using English-language MBTI Form M, published during 1999–2024. It reported favorable internal-consistency estimates (0.845–0.921) and convergent evidence, while finding no independent structural-validity or test–retest studies in its eligible literature beyond the manual. Score consistency does not establish distinct natural types, validate A/T, or transfer to FermatMind. Both supportive findings and remaining gaps depend on the specific instrument and samples.

The situations and exercises on this page are original educational examples, not clinical guidance or findings about groups. Compare them with your experience, including counterexamples. Do not use type alone to diagnose, hire, choose a career or screen a relationship.

Content revised 5 October 2026. This is a source-based educational synthesis, not a claim of independent clinical review.
